tasks.title: Mend the hours on one hill
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 1` in `hill_report.py`, `hill_hours` should give back the hours spent on one hill, added up, as a whole number. It calls `total_hours`, which calls `add_hours`, and the last line of the task stops with a `TypeError`. Run the file, read the traceback from the bottom up, and mend the one function where the mistake is. Leave the other two as they came with the file.

Check calls `hill_hours` with logs and hills of its own, a hill with no callout among them, and looks at what it gives back. It also looks at which functions you changed: only the one with the mistake.
nextSteps: Run `python3 hill_report.py` and read the last line of the traceback: the kind of error and its message.
Read the File line just above it: that is where Python stopped, and what it was doing there.
Go up one File line at a time and ask where each value came from.
Mend the function that made the wrong value, and run the file again.
hints: The last File line is `add_hours`, and its message says `+` met a whole number and text. `add_hours` adds what it is given; ask where the text came from.
`total_hours` hands on each value of the list it is given. The list is built in `hill_hours`, from parts of the log entries, and every part of a split text is text.
In `hill_hours`, the hours go into the list as text. Turn them into a whole number with `int(hours)` as they go in: `int` does not mind the spaces around the digits.

tasks.title: Mend the weight of a pack
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 2`, `pack_weight` takes the weights of the kit, a dictionary, and a packing list: kinds of kit with commas between them and spaces around some of the commas, such as `"rope, stretcher, first aid kit"`. It should give back what the kit on the list weighs, added up. It calls `weights_of`, which calls `weight_of`, and the last line of the task stops with a `KeyError`. Mend the one function where the mistake is, and leave the other two as they came.

Check calls `pack_weight` with weights and packing lists of its own, spaces in other places among them, and looks at what it gives back and at which functions you changed.
nextSteps: Run the file and read the message of the `KeyError`: it is the key that was not found.
Look at that key letter by letter, the quotes around it included.
Follow the File lines up to where that key was made.
Mend that function so every kind arrives without spaces at its ends.
hints: The message of a `KeyError` is the key itself, in quotes. Look inside the quotes: is that exactly a kind in the weights?
`weight_of` and `weights_of` only hand the kinds on. The kinds are cut out of the packing list in `pack_weight`, and splitting at a comma keeps the spaces next to it.
In `pack_weight`, go through the parts of `packing_list.split(",")` and keep each one stripped, in a new list. Then hand that list to `weights_of`.

tasks.title: Mend where the teams were
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 3`, `team_positions` takes the path of a JSON file, as text, and should give back what the file holds, as a dictionary. It calls `parse_positions`, which calls `json.loads`, and the last line of the task stops with an error from inside the `json` module. The file `positions.json` is fine. Find the last line of the traceback that is in your file, and mend the one function where the mistake is. Leave `parse_positions` as it came.

Check makes JSON files of its own in a copy of your workspace, calls `team_positions` with each one's path, and looks at what it gives back and at which function you changed.
nextSteps: Run the file. The File lines at the bottom are in the json module: skip them, up to the last line in `hill_report.py`.
Read what that line gives to `json.loads`.
Go up one more File line and look at what is handed to `parse_positions` there.
Mend that line and run the file again.
hints: A File line whose path is not `hill_report.py` is Python's own code. It stopped there because of what your code gave it, so look for the last File line that is in your file.
`json.loads` turns a text of JSON into Python values. Ask what text it was given: the line and column in the message count in that text.
`team_positions` reads the file into `text`, then hands `path` to `parse_positions`. Hand it `text`.
